What is wrong with treating a stationary saddle point as the global ground state?

A vanishing gradient only establishes stationarity. Check stability to the allowed orbital variations and compare relevant solutions; neither stationarity nor local stability establishes the global minimum.

写一个可运行的 Python 小例子，演示Rayleigh–Ritz 子空间残差，明确设置并加入必要数值检查。

以下是已在 PySCF 2.6.2 上运行通过的教学例子；具体结果由运行返回。
```python
import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import eigh
from pyscf import gto, scf, mp, cc, mcscf, ao2mo

def rayleigh_ritz():
    h = np.diag([0., 1., 3., 6.]) + 0.05*np.ones((4, 4))
    trial = np.array([[1., 0.], [0.2, 1.], [0.1, 0.3], [0.4, 0.2]])
    q, _ = np.linalg.qr(trial)
    projected = q.T @ h @ q
    energies, vectors = np.linalg.eigh(projected)
    vector = q @ vectors[:, 0]
    residual = h @ vector - energies[0] * vector
    exact = np.linalg.eigvalsh(h)[0]
    assert energies[0] >= exact - 1e-12
    assert np.linalg.norm(q.T @ residual) < 1e-12
    return dict(ritz_energy=float(energies[0]), exact_lowest=float(exact),
                full_residual=float(np.linalg.norm(residual)), projected_residual=float(np.linalg.norm(q.T @ residual)))

print(rayleigh_ritz())
```
